site.title: Snapmaker Studio guide — decide what to do with your project
site.description: A task-first guide to Snapmaker Studio v1.5.1: follow one example from opening a project to checking a sliced job, find help for what you are doing now, or look up a warning.
site.disclaimer: Snapmaker Studio is an **independent open-source project — not affiliated with or endorsed by Snapmaker**. “Snapmaker” is a trademark of its owner.
site.footer: This guide describes **Snapmaker Studio v1.5.1**, the current stable release. Studio is advisory: it checks and prepares files, Snapmaker Orca slices, and nothing here promises that a print will succeed. Source, release notes and verification: [github.com/DVOpenLabs/snapmaker-studio](@repo).

confirmed.label: Confirmed
confirmed.means: Studio has direct evidence: it read this in your file or from your printer, or you confirmed it yourself. The finding says which. It is a fact, not a guess.

check.label: Worth checking
check.means: Studio found something that may matter. Decide whether it does for this print.

unknown.label: Unknown
unknown.means: Studio could not establish this from what it has. It does not mean a problem was found; it is a gap for you to fill.

ok.label: Looks right
ok.means: Studio checked and found nothing wrong. Still advice, never a guarantee.

info.label: Good to know
info.means: Explains what Studio did or what a screen shows. Nothing to fix.
